turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - nlo_shg_eg_train.csv: 200 crystalline materials, columns `formula`,
    `poscar` (the crystal structure, in POSCAR format), `shg` (the largest
    SHG tensor component |d_ij|, in pm/V) and `band_gap` (the band gap, in
    eV).
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the LARGEST SHG tensor
component |d_ij| (pm/V) that also satisfy a transparency requirement: the
band gap must be at least 3 eV. Band gaps are NOT given for the pool -- you
must infer them. A selected candidate whose band gap is below the threshold
scores zero.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The training data exhibit a clear SHG–gap trade-off: the largest tensor components occur for small-gap chalcogenides (especially selenides/tellurides and pnictides), while every example with \(E_g\ge 3\) eV has \(|d_{ij}|\lesssim 19\) pm V\(^{-1}\).  The highest-gap, still-respectable SHG values belong to tetrahedrally coordinated sulfides (ZnS polytypes \(\approx 15\), CdGa\(_2\)S\(_4\) \(=21.7\) at \(2.86\) eV, ZnAgPS \(=18.5\) at \(3.34\) eV, LiSbS \(\approx 13\) at \(3.05\) eV).

Consequently the pool was screened for acentric, tetrahedral S- or light-Se-based structures whose cation chemistry is expected to keep the DFT gap above the 3 eV threshold:

- ZnGa\(_2\)S\(_4\) (c050–c052) is the direct Zn analogue of the training CdGa\(_2\)S\(_4\) entry.  The smaller Zn cation opens the gap by \(\sim 0.3\)–\(0.4\) eV while the SHG remains in the 18–21 pm V\(^{-1}\) range; the cell metrics of c051 are essentially identical to the training compound, so it is ranked first.
- Zinc-blende BeSe (c037) is the lightest II–VI selenide.  Scaling from the training ZnSe (\(E_g=2.0\) eV, \(|d|=28\)) and MgTe (\(E_g=3.23\) eV, \(|d|=10\)) entries places its gap comfortably above 3 eV and its SHG near 12–15 pm V\(^{-1}\).
- The mixed tetrahedral sulfide Al\(_2\)Zn\(_2\)S\(_5\) (c081) interpolates between training ZnS (\(\approx 15\)) and Al\(_2\)S\(_3\) (\(4.8\) at \(3.88\) eV), yielding an estimated \(|d|\approx 12\) pm V\(^{-1}\) and \(E_g>3.5\) eV.

All other high-SHG pool entries (selenides, phosphides, arsenides, iodides) are predicted to fall below the gap cutoff and therefore score zero.  The five compounds above are therefore the only candidates that simultaneously maximise SHG and satisfy the transparency constraint.

Final: c051, c052, c050, c037, c081
